Does z-scoring sex differences trajectories by a single lifespan male SD (as in
`fit_cv_mods_test.R`) compresses sex differences early in life, when structures are small?
This simulation tests that, and more generally asks which standardization supports:

1. integrals of sex difference trajectories that are comparable across phenotypes (Fig 2E&F,
i.e. "how biased towards a sex is this phenotype?"
2. classifying each phenotype's trajectory as converging vs diverging (Fig 3),
i.e. "are sex differences getting bigger or smaller over time?"
3. plotting sex difference trajectories on a common y axis (Extended Figs)

**Approach:** simulate phenotypes where the true sex difference is known, fit models, then compare each standardization against the truth.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#LOAD PACKAGES
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(gamlss)
library(ggplot2)
library(data.table)
library(pracma)
library(gamlssTools)

#shared sex-difference functions: get_deriv(), centile_sd()
source("../sex_diff_funs.R")

out_dir <- params$out_dir
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(file.path(out_dir, "centile_plots"), showWarnings = FALSE)
```

# Simulation settings

Every simulated phenotype follows a BCTo distribution with constant nu and tau. Sigma (~CV)
changes with age (see "Male sigma" below). Because sigma is ~CV, the SD scales with the median:
a structure that is 20x larger in adulthood is also ~20x more variable in raw units, on top of
any change in sigma itself.

```{r}
seed <- 20261022
n <- 4000         #sample size per simulated phenotype
sig <- 0.10       #default adult BCTo sigma (~CV); scenarios can set a different level
nu_true <- 0.5    #BCTo skewness, constant
tau_true <- 10    #BCTo kurtosis (t degrees of freedom), constant
```


```{r}
birth <- log10(280)
min_age <- log10(100)               #~mid-gestation
max_age <- log10(80 * 365.25 + 280) #80 years
ref_age <- log10(280 + 25 * 365.25) #25 years (ref point for testing male SD at specific age)

#axis labels in years for plots
age_breaks <- log10(c(150, 280, 280 + 365.25, 280 + 5 * 365.25, 280 + 20 * 365.25, 280 + 80 * 365.25))
age_labels <- c("-0.4", "0", "1", "5", "20", "80")
```

# True trajectories

## Male median

A sigmoid growth curve on log age, with a mild decline after age 30. `base` is fetal size
and `amp` is how much the structure grows to adulthood, so `base = 50, amp = 1000` grows ~20x
and `base = 500, amp = 500` grows ~2x.

```{r}
mu_male <- function(logAge, base = 50, amp = 1000) {
  base + amp * plogis((logAge - log10(280 + 2 * 365.25)) / 0.25) -
    0.08 * amp * pmax(logAge - log10(280 + 30 * 365.25), 0) / (max_age - log10(280 + 30 * 365.25))
}

grid_plot <- seq(min_age, max_age, length.out = 300)
data.frame(logAge_days = grid_plot,
           `High growth (~20x)` = mu_male(grid_plot, 50, 1000),
           `Low growth (~2x)` = mu_male(grid_plot, 500, 500),
           check.names = FALSE) %>%
  pivot_longer(-logAge_days, names_to = "phenotype") %>%
  ggplot(aes(logAge_days, value, color = phenotype)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = birth, color = "gray50", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = age_breaks, labels = age_labels) +
  expand_limits(y = 0) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "True male median", color = NULL) +
  theme_linedraw()
```

## Male sigma

Sigma increases with age: ~60% of its adult level prenatally, rising through childhood to its
adult level (i.e. value at age ~ 25), then rising again to ~140% by age 80. `level` is the phenotype's adult sigma.
Age 25 setpoint (`level`) defines low-variability phenotype vs a high-variability one.

```{r}
sigma_age <- function(logAge, level = sig) {
  level * (0.6 + 0.4 * plogis((logAge - log10(280 + 2 * 365.25)) / 0.25) +
             0.4 * plogis((logAge - log10(280 + 60 * 365.25)) / 0.05))
}

data.frame(logAge_days = grid_plot,
           `Low sigma (0.05)` = sigma_age(grid_plot, 0.05),
           `Default sigma (0.10)` = sigma_age(grid_plot, 0.10),
           `High sigma (0.20)` = sigma_age(grid_plot, 0.20),
           check.names = FALSE) %>%
  pivot_longer(-logAge_days, names_to = "level") %>%
  mutate(level = factor(level, levels = c("Low sigma (0.05)", "Default sigma (0.10)",
                                          "High sigma (0.20)"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(logAge_days, value, color = level)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = birth, color = "gray50", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = age_breaks, labels = age_labels) +
  expand_limits(y = 0) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "True male sigma (~CV)", color = NULL) +
  theme_linedraw()
```

## Sex difference

Each function returns the female deficit as a proportion of the male median at each age,
so female median = male median × (1 − effect).

- **A (`prop_effect`):** a constant 9% difference every age. The true log ratio is constant, so under the
  relative definition this is *neither* converging nor diverging. However, defining effects in terms of
  size is *not* constant: it is largest early in life, when sigma is lowest, and shrinks as
  sigma increases with age (i.e. male and female distributions overlap more, despite means being "farther" away).
- **B (`pubertal_effect`):** no difference until ~12 years, then 9%. Diverging under any metric.
- **C (`early_effect`):** 15% early in life, shrinking to 3% in adulthood. The *relative*
  difference converges, but the *absolute* difference still grows because the structure grows.
- **D (`late_drop_effect`):** 3% early, rising to 12% through childhood, then dropping back to
  3% after ~65. Diverges over most of the lifespan and converges only at the very end.

```{r}
prop_effect <- function(logAge) rep(0.09, length(logAge))
pubertal_effect <- function(logAge) 0.09 * plogis((logAge - log10(280 + 12 * 365.25)) / 0.04)
early_effect <- function(logAge) 0.03 + 0.12 * (1 - plogis((logAge - log10(280 + 2 * 365.25)) / 0.15))
late_drop_effect <- function(logAge) 0.03 + 0.09 * plogis((logAge - log10(280 + 10 * 365.25)) / 0.05) -
  0.09 * plogis((logAge - log10(280 + 70 * 365.25)) / 0.02)

data.frame(logAge_days = grid_plot,
           A = prop_effect(grid_plot),
           B = pubertal_effect(grid_plot),
           C = early_effect(grid_plot),
           D = late_drop_effect(grid_plot)) %>%
  pivot_longer(-logAge_days, names_to = "scenario") %>%
  ggplot(aes(logAge_days, value * 100, color = scenario)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = birth, color = "gray50", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = age_breaks, labels = age_labels) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "True male advantage (% of male median)", color = "Scenario") +
  theme_linedraw()
```

## Sex difference in sigma

Like the median sex difference, each function returns the female deficit as a proportion of
the male sigma at each age, so female sigma = male sigma × (1 − effect). Positive means males
are more variable. The true `logcv_M_div_F` is then log(sigma_M / sigma_F) = −log(1 − effect).

- **`sig_pubertal`:** none until ~12 years, then female sigma 10% lower. Diverging.
- **`sig_none`:** no sex difference in variability at any age. A null case.
- **`sig_early`:** female sigma 15% lower early in life, shrinking to 3% lower in adulthood. Converging.
- **`sig_constant`:** female sigma 5% lower at every age. Constant.

Because BCTo's median is ~mu regardless of sigma, these don't change the true median sex
difference. They also don't change any metric standardized by the *male* SD.

```{r}
sig_pubertal <- function(logAge) 0.10 * plogis((logAge - log10(280 + 12 * 365.25)) / 0.04)
sig_none <- function(logAge) rep(0, length(logAge))
sig_early <- function(logAge) 0.03 + 0.12 * (1 - plogis((logAge - log10(280 + 2 * 365.25)) / 0.15))
sig_constant <- function(logAge) rep(0.05, length(logAge))

data.frame(logAge_days = grid_plot,
           sig_pubertal = sig_pubertal(grid_plot),
           sig_none = sig_none(grid_plot),
           sig_early = sig_early(grid_plot),
           sig_constant = sig_constant(grid_plot)) %>%
  pivot_longer(-logAge_days, names_to = "pattern") %>%
  ggplot(aes(logAge_days, value * 100, color = pattern)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = birth, color = "gray50", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "gray50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = age_breaks, labels = age_labels) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "True female sigma deficit (% of male sigma)", color = NULL) +
  theme_linedraw()
```


## Scenarios

Scenario A is run as two pairs of phenotypes that share the same relative sex difference (9%):

- **Growth pair** (`A_high_growth`, `A_low_growth`): same sigma, different growth (~20x vs ~2x).
  The relative difference *and* the effect size are the same for both, so a metric that is
  comparable across phenotypes should give them the same integral.
- **Sigma pair** (`A_low_sigma`, `A_high_sigma`): same growth, adult sigma of 0.05 vs 0.20.
  The relative difference is the same, but the effect size is 4x larger in the low-sigma
  phenotype. Which one counts as "the same" depends on whether you mean relative to size or
  relative to variability, so metrics are expected to disagree here.

Each scenario also gets a sex difference in sigma (`sig_sex_fun`), so all four sigma patterns
appear: the A phenotypes diverge, B has none, C converges and D is constant.

New scenarios go at the end of the list, so existing scenarios keep their seeds.

```{r}
scenarios <- list(
  A_high_growth = list(sex_fun = prop_effect,     base = 50,  amp = 1000, sig = sig,  sig_sex_fun = sig_pubertal), #~20x growth
  A_low_growth  = list(sex_fun = prop_effect,     base = 500, amp = 500,  sig = sig,  sig_sex_fun = sig_pubertal), #~2x growth
  B_pubertal    = list(sex_fun = pubertal_effect, base = 50,  amp = 1000, sig = sig,  sig_sex_fun = sig_none),
  C_early_shrinking = list(sex_fun = early_effect, base = 50, amp = 1000, sig = sig,  sig_sex_fun = sig_early),
  D_late_drop   = list(sex_fun = late_drop_effect, base = 50, amp = 1000, sig = sig,  sig_sex_fun = sig_constant),
  A_low_sigma   = list(sex_fun = prop_effect,     base = 50,  amp = 1000, sig = 0.05, sig_sex_fun = sig_pubertal),
  A_high_sigma  = list(sex_fun = prop_effect,     base = 50,  amp = 1000, sig = 0.20, sig_sex_fun = sig_pubertal)
)
```

# Step by step for one scenario

Each step below is a function, run once on scenario A (high growth) so you can see its output.
The next section runs all of them on every scenario.

## 1. Simulate data

Ages are sampled to roughly mimic a lifespan dataset: 15% prenatal, 85% postnatal, uniform on
log age. Each scenario gets its own seed, so results don't depend on the order scenarios run in.

```{r}
sim_one <- function(spec, scen_seed) {
  set.seed(scen_seed)
  logAge <- c(runif(n * 0.15, min_age, birth),
              runif(n * 0.85, birth, max_age))
  sexMale <- rbinom(length(logAge), 1, 0.5)
  mu <- mu_male(logAge, spec$base, spec$amp) * (1 - (1 - sexMale) * spec$sex_fun(logAge))
  sigma <- sigma_age(logAge, spec$sig) * (1 - (1 - sexMale) * spec$sig_sex_fun(logAge))
  #BCTo: mu is the median, matching the real models
  y <- rBCTo(length(logAge), mu = mu, sigma = sigma, nu = nu_true, tau = tau_true)
  data.frame(y, logAge_days = logAge, sexMale = factor(sexMale),
             sexMale_x_logAge = sexMale * logAge)
}

demo_scen <- "A_high_growth"
demo_seed <- seed + match(demo_scen, names(scenarios))
demo_df <- sim_one(scenarios[[demo_scen]], demo_seed)

ggplot(demo_df, aes(logAge_days, y, color = sexMale)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, size = 0.6) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = age_breaks, labels = age_labels) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("0" = "#F4A15B", "1" = "#8CB3D1"), labels = c("Female", "Male")) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Simulated phenotype", color = NULL, title = demo_scen) +
  theme_linedraw()
```

## 2. Fit the model

```{r}
fit_model <- function(df) {
  gamlss(y ~ pb(sexMale_x_logAge) + pb(logAge_days) + sexMale,
         sigma.formula = ~ pb(sexMale_x_logAge) + pb(logAge_days) + sexMale,
         family = BCTo, data = df,
         control = gamlss.control(n.cyc = 400, trace = FALSE))
}

demo_model <- fit_model(demo_df)
```

## 2b. Centile fan plot

Same plot as `fit_cv_mods_test.R`, saved to `centile_plots/` in `out_dir` for every scenario.
Newer gamlssTools renamed `sim_data()` / `sim_data_list` to `sim_grid()` / `sim_grid_list`,
so this works with either version. `sexMale` is a factor here, so the special term converts it
to numeric.

```{r}
#gamlssTools version differences: sim_data -> sim_grid, sim_data_list -> sim_grid_list
sim_fun <- if (exists("sim_grid", envir = asNamespace("gamlssTools"))) sim_grid else sim_data
sim_arg <- if ("sim_grid_list" %in% names(formals(make_centile_fan))) "sim_grid_list" else "sim_data_list"

save_fan_plot <- function(model, df, scen) {
  sim_df <- sim_fun(df, "logAge_days", factor_var = "sexMale",
                    special_term = "sexMale_x_logAge = as.numeric(as.character(sexMale)) * logAge_days")

  fan_args <- list(gamlssModel = model,
                   df = df,
                   x_var = "logAge_days",
                   color_var = "sexMale",
                   get_peaks = TRUE,
                   desiredCentiles = c(0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95),
                   show_points = TRUE,
                   label_centiles = "legend",
                   point_color_manual = c('0' = "#F4A15BFF", '1' = "#8CB3D1FF"),
                   color_manual = c("0" = "#c05f0d", "1" = "#38688D"),
                   x_axis = "log_lifespan_fetal")
  fan_args[[sim_arg]] <- sim_df

  fan_plot <- do.call(make_centile_fan, fan_args) +
    theme_linedraw() +
    scale_color_manual(name = "Sex",
                       values = c('0' = "#c05f0d", '1' = "#38688D"),
                       labels = c("Female", "Male")) +
    guides(fill = "none",
           fill_ggnewscale_1 = "none", colour_ggnewscale_1 = "none") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = birth, color = "gray20", linetype = "dashed") +
    labs(title = paste(scen, "simulated model"),
         x = "Age (years)")

  ggsave(file = file.path(out_dir, "centile_plots", paste0(scen, ".png")), fan_plot,
         width = 8, height = 5)
  fan_plot
}

save_fan_plot(demo_model, demo_df, demo_scen)
```

## 3. Predict on an age grid

For each sex, predict the median (mu) and sigma at 300 evenly spaced log ages, plus the male SD.

The SD is a centile-based approximation, computed by `centile_sd()` in `sex_diff_funs.R` from
the fitted BCTo distribution at each age, as in `process_sex_diffs()`: the interquartile range
divided by 1.349, which equals the SD for a normal distribution (the semi-interquartile range,
Rigby et al. 2019 sec 2.3). Unlike the moment-based SD, it exists even when heavy tails (small
tau, especially with negative nu) make the variance infinite.

```{r}
grid <- seq(min_age, max_age, length.out = 300)

predict_grid <- function(model, df) {
  lapply(c("0", "1"), function(s) {
    nd <- data.frame(logAge_days = grid, sexMale = factor(s, levels = c("0", "1")),
                     sexMale_x_logAge = as.numeric(s) * grid)
    p <- predictAll(model, newdata = nd, type = "response", data = df)
    data.frame(logAge_days = grid, sex = ifelse(s == "1", "Male", "Female"),
               med = p$mu,
               sigma = p$sigma,
               sd = centile_sd("BCTo", p$mu, p$sigma, p$nu, p$tau))
  }) %>%
    bind_rows() %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = sex, values_from = c(med, sigma, sd))
}

demo_pred <- predict_grid(demo_model, demo_df)
head(demo_pred)
```

## 4. Standardize the sex difference

Every metric is computed from the fitted curves, along with its true counterpart (`true_*`):

| Column | Formula | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `pooled_z` | (med_M − med_F) / SD(all male y) | Current method in `fit_cv_mods_test.R` |
| `age_z` | (med_M − med_F) / SD_M(age) | Effect size at each age |
| `ref_z` | (med_M − med_F) / SD_M(age 25) | Standardized relative to one adult SD per phenotype |
| `log_ratio` | log(med_M / med_F) | Relative difference (analogous to current method for sigma) |
| `raw_diff` | med_M − med_F | Unstandardized difference trajectory |
| `peak_scaled` | raw_diff / max\|raw_diff\| × 100 | % of the phenotype's peak difference |
| `logcv_ratio` | log(sigma_M / sigma_F) | Sex difference in variability (`logcv_M_div_F`) |

```{r}
add_metrics <- function(pred, df, spec, scen) {
  #POOLED z-score: single lifespan male SD (current method in preprint)
  std_dev_pheno <- sd(df$y[df$sexMale == 1])

  #fitted male SD at the reference age
  ref_sd <- approx(pred$logAge_days, pred$sd_Male, xout = ref_age)$y

  #truth on the same grid
  true_M <- mu_male(grid, spec$base, spec$amp)
  true_F <- true_M * (1 - spec$sex_fun(grid))
  true_sd_M <- centile_sd("BCTo", true_M, sigma_age(grid, spec$sig), nu_true, tau_true)

  pred %>%
    mutate(scenario = scen,
           true_age_z = (true_M - true_F) / true_sd_M,
           pooled_z = (med_Male - med_Female) / std_dev_pheno,
           age_z = (med_Male - med_Female) / sd_Male,
           ref_z = (med_Male - med_Female) / ref_sd,
           log_ratio = log(med_Male / med_Female),
           raw_diff = med_Male - med_Female,
           true_log_ratio = log(true_M / true_F),
           true_raw_diff = true_M - true_F,
           true_pooled_z = true_raw_diff / std_dev_pheno,
           true_ref_z = true_raw_diff / centile_sd("BCTo", mu_male(ref_age, spec$base, spec$amp),
                                                   sigma_age(ref_age, spec$sig), nu_true, tau_true),
           peak_scaled = raw_diff / max(abs(raw_diff)) * 100,
           true_peak_scaled = true_raw_diff / max(abs(true_raw_diff)) * 100,
           logcv_ratio = log(sigma_Male / sigma_Female),
           true_logcv_ratio = -log(1 - spec$sig_sex_fun(grid)),
           #how much smaller the pooled z is than the age-specific z
           compression = pooled_z / age_z,
           pooled_sd = std_dev_pheno,
           ref_sd = ref_sd)
}

demo_res <- add_metrics(demo_pred, demo_df, scenarios[[demo_scen]], demo_scen)
demo_res %>%
  select(logAge_days, true_age_z, pooled_z, age_z, ref_z, log_ratio, true_log_ratio) %>%
  slice(seq(1, n(), by = 50))
```

# Run every scenario

This fits one model per scenario, so it takes a few minutes. Each model's centile fan plot is
saved to `centile_plots/<scenario>.png` in `out_dir`.

```{r}
run_scenario <- function(scen) {
  print(paste("scenario", scen))
  spec <- scenarios[[scen]]
  df <- sim_one(spec, seed + match(scen, names(scenarios)))
  model <- fit_model(df)
  save_fan_plot(model, df, scen)
  pred <- predict_grid(model, df)
  add_metrics(pred, df, spec, scen)
}

res <- bind_rows(lapply(names(scenarios), run_scenario))
fwrite(res, file.path(out_dir, "zscore_sim_results.csv"))
```

# Does a single SD compress early-life differences?

## Values at landmark ages

`compression` is `pooled_z / age_z`: how much smaller the current metric (standardize by one lifespan SD) makes the sex
difference than an age-specific effect size. `true_age_z` is the true value of `age_z`; it is the
reference here because the reviewer's claim is about compression relative to a within-age
effect size, not because it is the only valid target.

```{r}
metrics <- c("true_age_z", "pooled_z", "age_z", "ref_z", "log_ratio", "true_log_ratio",
             "raw_diff", "peak_scaled", "true_peak_scaled", "logcv_ratio", "true_logcv_ratio")

landmarks <- c("mid-gestation" = log10(150), "birth" = birth,
               "1 yr" = log10(280 + 365.25), "5 yr" = log10(280 + 5 * 365.25),
               "15 yr" = log10(280 + 15 * 365.25), "40 yr" = log10(280 + 40 * 365.25),
               "75 yr" = log10(280 + 75 * 365.25))
summ <- lapply(names(landmarks), function(l) {
  res %>%
    group_by(scenario) %>%
    slice_min(abs(logAge_days - landmarks[[l]]), n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(age = l)
}) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  select(scenario, age, all_of(metrics), compression) %>%
  arrange(scenario, match(age, names(landmarks))) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
#fwrite(summ, file.path(out_dir, "zscore_sim_landmarks.csv"))

knitr::kable(summ %>% select(scenario, age, true_age_z, age_z, pooled_z, compression))
```


```{r, fig.height=15}
plot_df <- res %>%
  select(scenario, logAge_days, true_age_z, age_z, pooled_z) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(true_age_z, age_z, pooled_z), names_to = "metric") %>%
  mutate(metric = recode(metric,
                         true_age_z = "Truth (standardized to age-specific SD)",
                         age_z = "Fitted, age-specific SD",
                         pooled_z = "Fitted, single lifespan SD (current)"))

p <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(logAge_days, value, color = metric, linetype = metric)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = birth, color = "gray50", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~ scenario, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = age_breaks, labels = age_labels) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Truth (standardized to age-specific SD)" = "black",
                                "Fitted, age-specific SD" = "#38688D",
                                "Fitted, single lifespan SD (current)" = "#c05f0d")) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Truth (standardized to age-specific SD)" = "dotted",
                                   "Fitted, age-specific SD" = "solid",
                                   "Fitted, single lifespan SD (current)" = "solid")) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Male - Female (SD units)", color = NULL, linetype = NULL,
       title = "Sex difference standardized by single vs age-specific male SD") +
  theme_linedraw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "zscore_sim.png"), p, width = 8, height = 15)
p
```

Takeaway - z-scoring by a single SD value calculated from the lifespan distribution does compress trajectories
at all ages relative to standardizing against an age-specific SD, young ages most of all.

# Aim 1: integrals comparable across phenotypes

## Integrals

Each integral is divided by the age span so it reads as the average sex difference over age.
Taking the Riemann-Stieltjes integral over log-age to rescale it to regular age in days.

The last two columns compare each pair:

- `high_div_low_growth`: the growth pair has the same relative difference and the same effect
  size, so a metric that is comparable across phenotypes should give ~1.
- `low_div_high_sigma`: the sigma pair has the same relative difference but a 4x different
  effect size. Relative metrics should give ~1; effect-size metrics should give ~4.
  
`age_z` ~ "how separable are the sexes' distributions?"
`log_ratio` ~ "how big is the male median relative to the female median?"

```{r}
#left Riemann-Stieltjes integral over raw age, as in test_rs_integral.R
rs_integral <- function(x, y, g = function(x) 10^(x)) {
  stopifnot(length(x) == length(y), length(x) >= 2)
  ord <- order(x); x <- x[ord]; y <- y[ord]
  gx <- g(x)
  if (any(diff(gx) < 0)) stop("g(x) must be non-decreasing for a Riemann-Stieltjes integral")
  sum(y[-length(y)] * diff(gx))
}

span_raw <- 10^max_age - 10^min_age
integrals <- res %>%
  group_by(scenario) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(metrics), ~ rs_integral(logAge_days, .x) / span_raw),
          pooled_sd = first(pooled_sd), ref_sd = first(ref_sd)) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(scenario, pooled_sd, ref_sd), names_to = "metric") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = scenario, values_from = value, id_cols = metric)  %>%
  mutate(high_div_low_growth = A_high_growth / A_low_growth,
         low_div_high_sigma = A_low_sigma / A_high_sigma) %>%
  arrange(match(metric, metrics)) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
fwrite(integrals, file.path(out_dir, "zscore_sim_integrals.csv"))

knitr::kable(integrals %>%
  select(metric,high_div_low_growth, low_div_high_sigma))
```

## Phenotype pairs under each standardization

If a metric treats a pair as equal, the two lines overlap.

```{r}
#plot one pair of phenotypes under each standardization
#pair_labels: named vector, names = scenarios, values = legend labels
plot_pair <- function(pair_labels, title) {
  pair_df <- res %>%
    filter(scenario %in% names(pair_labels)) %>%
    select(scenario, logAge_days, pooled_z, age_z, ref_z, log_ratio, peak_scaled) %>%
    pivot_longer(c(pooled_z, age_z, ref_z, log_ratio, peak_scaled), names_to = "metric") %>%
    mutate(metric = factor(recode(metric,
                                  pooled_z = "Single lifespan SD (current)",
                                  age_z = "Age-specific SD",
                                  ref_z = "SD at age 25",
                                  log_ratio = "log(M / F)",
                                  peak_scaled = "Scaled to peak (%)"),
                           levels = c("Single lifespan SD (current)", "Age-specific SD",
                                      "SD at age 25", "log(M / F)", "Scaled to peak (%)")))

  ggplot(pair_df, aes(logAge_days, value, color = scenario)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = birth, color = "gray50", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
    facet_wrap(~ metric, ncol = 3, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = age_breaks, labels = age_labels) +
    scale_color_manual(values = setNames(c("#38688D", "#c05f0d"), names(pair_labels)),
                       labels = pair_labels) +
    expand_limits(y = 0) +
    labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Male - Female", color = NULL, title = title) +
    theme_linedraw() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}
```

# Aim 2: converging vs diverging

## Two lifespan-wide measures

**Current measure (`review_test_models.Rmd`):** square the sex difference (so larger means more
different, whatever the direction), take its derivative over log age, and integrate.
Negative means converging, positive means diverging.

Integrating a derivative just gives back the change in the original function, so over log age
this equals (squared difference at the oldest age) − (squared difference at the youngest age).
It only compares the two endpoints.

**Alternative:** the least-squares slope of |difference| over log age. It uses the whole curve,
gives the least weight to the endpoints, and isn't squared, so changes count the same whether
the sex difference is large or small.

Both are also expressed relative to the peak difference (`sq_int_rel`, `abs_slope_rel`). Changes
under 5% of the peak are flagged `~constant`.

```{r}
#get_deriv() comes from sex_diff_funs.R, as in the real pipeline

#log-age range, to express the slope as a change across the whole lifespan
span_log <- max_age - min_age

#fitted metric and its ground-truth counterpart
conv_metrics <- data.frame(
  label = c("Single lifespan SD (current)", "Raw difference", "Age-specific SD",
            "SD at age 25", "log(M / F)", "Scaled to peak (%)"),
  fitted = c("pooled_z", "raw_diff", "age_z", "ref_z", "log_ratio", "peak_scaled"),
  truth = c("true_pooled_z", "true_raw_diff", "true_age_z", "true_ref_z", "true_log_ratio",
            "true_peak_scaled")
)

#long format: one row per scenario x source (fitted/truth) x metric x age
conv_long <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(conv_metrics)), function(i) {
  bind_rows(
    res %>% mutate(source = "fitted", value = .data[[conv_metrics$fitted[i]]]),
    res %>% mutate(source = "truth", value = .data[[conv_metrics$truth[i]]])
  ) %>%
    mutate(metric = factor(conv_metrics$label[i], levels = conv_metrics$label)) %>%
    select(scenario, source, metric, logAge_days, value)
}) %>%
  bind_rows()

conv <- conv_long %>%
  group_by(scenario, source, metric) %>%
  arrange(logAge_days, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(sq = value^2,
         sq_deriv = get_deriv(sq, logAge_days)) %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  summarise(
    #review_test_models.Rmd line ~941: trapz over log age
    sq_int = trapz(logAge_days, sq_deriv),
    #review_test_models.Rmd line ~1049: integral over raw age
    sq_int.unlog = rs_integral(logAge_days, sq_deriv),
    #relative to the peak; 0 when there is no difference at any age (e.g. sig_none truth)
    sq_int_rel = ifelse(max(sq) > 0, sq_int / max(sq), 0),
    #raw-age version on the same scale: per day instead of per log unit, so a change spread
    #evenly over log age gives the same value as sq_int_rel
    sq_int.unlog_rel = ifelse(max(sq) > 0, sq_int.unlog / span_raw * span_log / max(sq), 0),
    #least-squares slope of |difference| over log age
    abs_slope = cov(logAge_days, abs(value)) / var(logAge_days),
    #change across the lifespan implied by the slope, relative to the peak |difference|
    abs_slope_rel = ifelse(max(abs(value)) > 0, abs_slope * span_log / max(abs(value)), 0),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(trajectory = ifelse(sq_int < 0, "converging", "diverging"),
         trajectory.unlog = ifelse(sq_int.unlog < 0, "converging", "diverging"),
         trajectory_tol = ifelse(abs(sq_int_rel) < 0.05, "~constant", trajectory),
         trajectory.unlog_tol = ifelse(abs(sq_int.unlog_rel) < 0.05, "~constant", trajectory.unlog),
         slope_trajectory = case_when(abs(abs_slope_rel) < 0.05 ~ "~constant",
                                      abs_slope < 0 ~ "converging",
                                      TRUE ~ "diverging")) %>%
  arrange(scenario, source, metric)
fwrite(conv, file.path(out_dir, "zscore_sim_convergence.csv"))
```

## Does diverging/converging depend on the metric?

Endpoint integral (the current measure) for the fitted curves. `pooled_z`, `raw_diff`, `ref_z`
and `peak_scaled` differ only by a constant, so they always get the same call.

```{r}
conv %>%
  #filter(source == "fitted") %>%
  mutate(call = sprintf("%s (%+.2f)", trajectory_tol, sq_int_rel)) %>%
  select(scenario, metric, source, call) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = scenario, values_from = call) %>%
  arrange(metric) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

## Endpoint integral vs slope, for the log ratios

Compare each measure's fitted value to its truth. A measure that depends on the endpoints will
be thrown off where the model fits the ends of the age range poorly (e.g. scenario D's late drop).

Median, log(M / F):

```{r}
conv %>%
  filter(metric == "log(M / F)") %>%
  mutate(endpoint = sprintf("%s (%+.2f)", trajectory_tol, sq_int_rel),
         slope = sprintf("%s (%+.2f)", slope_trajectory, abs_slope_rel)) %>%
  select(scenario, source, endpoint, slope) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = source, values_from = c(endpoint, slope)) %>%
  knitr::kable()

conv %>%
  filter(metric == "Age-specific SD") %>%
  mutate(endpoint = sprintf("%s (%+.2f)", trajectory_tol, sq_int_rel),
         slope = sprintf("%s (%+.2f)", slope_trajectory, abs_slope_rel)) %>%
  select(scenario, source, endpoint, slope) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = source, values_from = c(endpoint, slope)) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

## What each measure sees

Each panel shows |sex difference| (black), the thing both measures summarize, with:

- **Least-squares line (blue):** its slope is `abs_slope`, in units of |difference| per tenfold
  increase in age. The blue arrow at the right is the line's total rise or fall across the age
  range (`abs_slope` × `span_log`).
- **Peak (gray dashed):** `abs_slope_rel` is the blue arrow's length divided by this peak.
- **Endpoints (orange):** the endpoint integral equals |difference|² at the oldest age minus
  |difference|² at the youngest, so only these two points matter. `sq_int_rel` divides that by
  the peak squared.

Change `slope_metric` to see a different metric.

```{r, fig.width=16, fig.height=8}
slope_metric <- "log(M / F)"
slope_scens <- c("A_high_growth", "B_pubertal", "C_early_shrinking", "D_late_drop")

#|difference| on the age grid, dropping each group's first age as conv does (na.omit after get_deriv)
slope_curve <- conv_long %>%
  filter(metric == slope_metric, scenario %in% slope_scens) %>%
  group_by(scenario, source) %>%
  arrange(logAge_days, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  slice(-1) %>%
  mutate(abs_value = abs(value)) %>%
  ungroup()

#least-squares line, endpoints and peak for each panel
slope_fit <- slope_curve %>%
  group_by(scenario, source) %>%
  summarise(slope = cov(logAge_days, abs_value) / var(logAge_days),
            intercept = mean(abs_value) - slope * mean(logAge_days),
            x0 = min(logAge_days), x1 = max(logAge_days),
            y_start = abs_value[which.min(logAge_days)],
            y_end = abs_value[which.max(logAge_days)],
            peak = max(abs_value),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(line0 = intercept + slope * x0,
         line1 = intercept + slope * x1) %>%
  left_join(conv %>% filter(metric == slope_metric),
            by = c("scenario", "source")) %>%
  mutate(label = sprintf("abs_slope = %+.3f / log10 age\nabs_slope_rel = %+.2f (%s)\nendpoint sq_int_rel = %+.2f (%s)",
                         abs_slope, abs_slope_rel, slope_trajectory, sq_int_rel, trajectory_tol))

p_slope <- ggplot(slope_curve, aes(logAge_days, abs_value)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = birth, color = "gray50", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(data = slope_fit, aes(yintercept = peak), color = "gray50", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(aes(color = "|difference|"), linewidth = 0.9) +
  #least-squares line and its total change across the age range
  geom_segment(data = slope_fit, aes(x = x0, xend = x1, y = line0, yend = line1,
                                     color = "Least-squares line"), linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_segment(data = slope_fit, aes(x = x0, xend = x1, y = line0, yend = line0),
               color = "#38688D", linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_segment(data = slope_fit, aes(x = x1, xend = x1, y = line0, yend = line1),
               color = "#38688D", arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.15, "cm"))) +
  #endpoints compared by the endpoint integral
  geom_segment(data = slope_fit, aes(x = x0, xend = x1, y = y_start, yend = y_end,
                                     color = "Endpoints"), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(data = slope_fit, aes(x = x0, y = y_start, color = "Endpoints"), size = 2) +
  geom_point(data = slope_fit, aes(x = x1, y = y_end, color = "Endpoints"), size = 2) +
  geom_label(data = slope_fit, aes(x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = label),
             hjust = -0.02, vjust = 1.05, size = 2.8, label.size = 0, alpha = 0.8) +
  facet_grid(source ~ scenario, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = age_breaks, labels = age_labels) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.6))) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("|difference|" = "black", "Least-squares line" = "#38688D",
                                "Endpoints" = "#c05f0d")) + 
  expand_limits(y = 0) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = paste0("|", slope_metric, "|"), color = NULL,
       title = paste("Slope vs endpoint convergence measures,", slope_metric)) +
  theme_linedraw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "zscore_sim_slope_vs_endpoint_agesd.png"), p_slope, width = 16, height = 8)
p_slope
```

## Log age vs raw age integral

`review_test_models.Rmd` computes the same derivative of the squared difference two ways:

- `trajectory` (`sq_int`): integrated over **log age** with `trapz`. This telescopes to
  (squared difference at the oldest age) − (squared difference at the youngest age).
- `trajectory.unlog` (`sq_int.unlog`): integrated over **raw age** with `rs_integral`. Each age's
  derivative is weighted by how many days it covers, and adulthood covers most of the days, so
  this mostly reflects the change over adulthood.

`sq_int.unlog_rel` puts the raw-age version on the same scale as `sq_int_rel` (divided by
days instead of log units, and by the peak squared), so both get the same 5% tolerance.

```{r}
conv %>%
  mutate(log_age = sprintf("%s (%+.2f)", trajectory_tol, sq_int_rel),
         raw_age = sprintf("%s (%+.2f)", trajectory.unlog_tol, sq_int.unlog_rel),
         agree = ifelse(trajectory_tol == trajectory.unlog_tol, "", "differ")) %>%
  select(scenario, source, metric, log_age, raw_age, agree) %>%
  arrange(metric, source, scenario) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

The plot shows where each integral builds up its value: the running total from the youngest
age to each age, scaled by its own largest absolute value so both fit one axis. The value at
the right edge is the final integral, and its sign is the call.

```{r, fig.width=16, fig.height=8}
#running totals of the same two integrals, for the slope_metric scenarios above
cum_df <- conv_long %>%
  filter(metric == slope_metric, scenario %in% slope_scens) %>%
  group_by(scenario, source) %>%
  arrange(logAge_days, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(sq_deriv = get_deriv(value^2, logAge_days)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(sq_deriv)) %>%
  #zero out floating-point noise, e.g. scenario A truth, where the true change is exactly 0
  mutate(sq_deriv = ifelse(abs(sq_deriv) < 1e-12, 0, sq_deriv),
         n_age = n(),
         #trapz over log age
         `Log age (trajectory)` = c(0, cumsum(diff(logAge_days) *
                                                (sq_deriv[-1] + sq_deriv[-n_age[1]]) / 2)),
         #left Riemann-Stieltjes sum over raw age, as rs_integral
         `Raw age (trajectory.unlog)` = c(0, cumsum(sq_deriv[-n_age[1]] * diff(10^logAge_days)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(`Log age (trajectory)`, `Raw age (trajectory.unlog)`),
               names_to = "integral", values_to = "running") %>%
  group_by(scenario, source, integral) %>%
  mutate(running = if (max(abs(running)) > 0) running / max(abs(running)) else 0) %>%
  ungroup()

p_unlog <- ggplot(cum_df, aes(logAge_days, running, color = integral)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = birth, color = "gray50", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "gray50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  facet_grid(source ~ scenario) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = age_breaks, labels = age_labels) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Log age (trajectory)" = "#c05f0d",
                                "Raw age (trajectory.unlog)" = "#38688D")) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Running integral (scaled to its largest |value|)", color = NULL,
       title = paste("Where each convergence integral builds up,", slope_metric)) +
  theme_linedraw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "zscore_sim_unlog_logmf.png"), p_unlog, width = 16, height = 8)
p_unlog
```
